newsitem.title: UK: UK Court to investigate damages for Nadir aide.
newsitem.headline: UK Court to investigate damages for Nadir aide.

text.p: A British court on Thursday ordered an investigation into possible damage suffered by former Asil Nadir aide Elizabeth Forsyth as a result of an injunction freezing her bank accounts.

The judge, Mr Justice Evans-Lombe, also ruled that the administrators of Polly Peck International, accountancy firm Deloitte & Touche, should pay indemnity costs to Forsyth, who has been using official legal aid, after they decided to drop the injunction.
The judge ordered the costs to be paid on an indemnity basis, the highest possible award.
"This is the last court case I hope, I've had three years of this, said Forsyth outside the court. "We are considering other actions, we are taking advice on that."
Earlier, the joint administrators of Polly Peck International said they had halted a civil action against Forsyth.

"A decision has been taken that for commercial reasons, the joint administrators do not at present consider it to be in the interests of the creditors to continue with their civil action in its present form and have therefore taken steps to discontinue it," Chris Morris of Deloitte & Touche said in a statement.

Morris said the administrators of Nadir's failed fruits-to-electronics empire had carefully considered the effect of Forsyth's successful appeal against a criminal conviction in reaching their decision.

In March Forsyth had her conviction for handling stolen money overturned by a London appeal court. She had already served 10 months of a five-year jail sentence for dishonestly handling 400,000 pounds ($670,000).
Forsyth was chairman of South Audley Management, a firm set up by Nadir to deal with his wealthy family businesses before the empire collapsed in 1990 under the weight of huge debts.
Nadir fled Britain for his native Northern Cyprus in 1993, skipping bail of 3.5 million pounds.

He has since travelled to Turkey but because Britain does not have an extradition treaty with Turkey has not been returned to face British justice. The Serious Fraud Office (SFO) still has a warrant for Nadir's arrest outstanding. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
